text: Different World is the debut studio album by Norwegian DJ and record producer Alan Walker, released on 14 December 2018 through MER Musikk and Sony Music Entertainment, and includes his successful 2015 single "Faded". The album follows a trilogy of singles titled World of Walker, consisting of "All Falls Down", "Darkside", and "Diamond Heart". It was nominated for Top Dance/Electronic Albums at the 2020 Billboard Music Awards. Featuring artists such as Steve Aoki, Noah Cyrus, and Digital Farm Animals, the album combines recognizable tracks like "Faded" with new material such as "Lost Control". Walker stated that releasing the album was an "incredible feeling" and described it as a significant milestone after years of work, expressing excitement to share it with fans. A campaign titled "#CreateADifferentWorld" was launched to raise awareness about climate change. The first single, "Faded", features uncredited Naustdal pop singer Iselin Solheim and was released on 3 December 2015; it reached number one in Austria, Germany, Switzerland, and Sweden, was nominated for British Single of the Year at the 2017 Brit Awards, and won Årets Låt (Song of the Year) at the Spellemannprisen. The second single, "Sing Me to Sleep", also featuring Iselin Solheim, was released on June 3, 2016, and reached number one in Norway and number one on the iTunes charts in seven countries. "Alone", featuring uncredited singer Noonie Bao, was released as the third single on December 2, 2016, and charted internationally, reaching number one on the Norwegian Singles Chart. "All Falls Down", featuring Noah Cyrus and Digital Farm Animals, was released as the fourth single on 27 October 2017 and peaked at number one on the Norwegian Singles Chart and the US Billboard Dance Club Songs chart. "Darkside", featuring Antiguan-German singer-songwriter Au/Ra and Norwegian singer Tomine Harket, was released as the fifth single on 27 July 2018, with a remix by Dutch DJ Afrojack that reached number one in Norway and number 10 in Sweden. "Diamond Heart", featuring Swedish singer-songwriter Sophia Somajo, was released as the sixth single on September 28, 2018, with official remixes by Syn Cole and Dzeko; its music video was nominated for Best Cinematography at the 2019 Berlin Music Video Awards. "Different World", featuring American singer Sofia Carson, Norwegian music producer K-391, and Chinese music producer Corsak, was released as the album's lead single on November 30, 2018, coinciding with the "#CreateADifferentWorld" campaign and includes Walker's commentary on climate change; it reached number 31 in the Norwegian charts. Dancing Astronaut described the album as extending the fullest portrait of Walker's distinctive sound and a tightly threaded collection of songs that showcases his sonic artistry. Billboard called it a project that turns bleating synth melodies into sing-alongs, melts warm Caribbean rhythms with hardstyle booms, and electrifies the dance floor while aiming for radio readiness. Manuel Probst of Dance-Charts [de] noted that Walker's typical sound design runs through the album like a common thread, creating a melancholy atmosphere with attention to detail allowing each song to have a unique touch. Marit Johansen Jegthaug of NRK P3 criticized the album for having too few new songs, poor structure, lack of variety, and a lack of distinction between old and new tracks. Tor Martin Bøe of Verdens Gang gave it a "die throw" rating of 3 out of 6, describing it as "manic and gloomy" and stating the dark sense of abandonment feels "almost tacked on". Anjali Raguraman of The Straits Times described it as a "cinematic, vocals-driven album" and noted that it feels like Walker has played it safe by sticking to his familiar style. At the time of Billboard's 2019 mid-year report, the album had 93,000 equivalent album sales in the United States and "Faded" had 192,396,000 streams. Sales figures are based on certification alone; sales+streaming figures are also based on certification alone.
